messages:
incident-bot: Pager - deploy.canary: High 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2 (growth from 0.2% -> 18% in 3m). Severity: P1. Links: https://ops.redwood.ai/incidents/1945670042
Anna: noticing spikes on dashboard, started 3m ago. can confirm 502 & 503s from inference-proxy.
Mike: I kicked off the canary ~20m ago (artifact v2.14.0). Canaries were 10%->50% when errors rose.
Lina: joining, oncall. can someone paste logs from proxy?
Anna: tail logs: 
```
2026-03-15T15:04:01Z proxy[container]: upstream error: KMS.DecryptFailed: AccessDenied
2026-03-15T15:04:02Z proxy[container]: failed to load env: unable to decrypt REPLICA_KEY
2026-03-15T15:04:02Z proxy[container]: returning 502 to client
```
Sam: who rotated keys today? we had a KMS rotation job for model-keys scheduled ~14:00 UTC via infra-cicd.
Mike: yep that was me — rotated key for project/redwood-prod/model-key and updated key version id in secrets manager. I thought deploy would pick it up.
Lina: ok likely root cause: during rollout new replicas attempt to decrypt secret with new key version but deploy service account doesn't have decrypt on the new key version. old pods still served fine.
Anna: traffic graph shows latency normal for older hosts, new hosts 502. can we kill the canary?
deploy-bot: Canary kill invoked by Anna at 1945670065. Rolling canary back to v2.13.9 -> traffic 100%.
Anna: flipping feature flag -> `ff.deploy_canary_allow=true` to false via console, but keeping read-only telemetry. :white_check_mark:
Mike: confirmed flagged off. canary traffic slumped, error rate dropped to baseline within 90s.
Lina: leaving wide open note: temporary mitigation = rollback / kill-switch. next step: fix KMS IAM for service-account used by deploy agents. Sam, can you check which SA made decrypt calls?
Sam: logs show serviceAccount: `redwood-deploy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` attempted decrypt and got PermissionDenied on key version projects/.../cryptoKeyVersions/7.
Anna: quick fix options: (A) grant roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter to that SA for the new key version, (B) revert secret to old key version, (C) force redeploy with mounted old secret. Which is least risky?
Mike: I'd prefer A (grant decrypt) so we avoid another rollback. but need to confirm org policy.
Lina: agree. Sam, apply minimal IAM binding scoped to that cryptoKey resource and test on a single canary host. Use principle of least privilege.
Sam: applying binding now: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding model-key \
  --location=global --keyring=prod-keys \
  --member=serviceAccount:redwood-deploy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
Sam: binding applied at 1945670220. testing one restarted canary pod...
Anna: restarted pod logs: 
```
2026-03-15T15:10:23Z proxy[container]: decrypt OK for REPLICA_KEY (key version 7)
2026-03-15T15:10:23Z proxy[container]: loaded env, starting worker
```
Lina: great. promote canary again only after 10m of green metrics. Recommend also adding automated permission check to preflight so future key rotations fail fast in CI.
Mike: agreed. I will also update infra-cicd rotation job to annotate key rotations and trigger an IAM add step if target SA missing decrypt.
Anna: customer impact summary for now: roughly 14% of customer requests for us-west-2 in the 8m window returned 5xx; majority were ingested by models behind canary. No SSO or data exfil detected.
Lina: action items (post-incident):
- Mike: update key-rotation job and include IA test (due EOD)
- Sam: add preflight IAM check to cicd + runbook (due tomorrow)
- Anna: draft customer-facing incident note & slack notify to accounts (due in 2h)
- Infra: add a canary preflight that verifies secret decryption on new key versions (ticket created)
Anna: handing off to Lina for next-period oncall, I'm going offline for meeting. Lina: take it. :wave:
Lina: taking handoff. watching green windows for 30m, will escalate if any regression.
incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 1945670442. Root cause: missing KMS decrypt permission for redeployed canary hosts after key rotation. Follow-up: postmortem scheduled, severity: P1 -> Rc (mitigated).
